questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines?

hints.nudge: It starts with the letter K and has 9 letters.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Saint Vincent and the Grenadines article.

questions.proof: The capital, and its main port, is Kingstown.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines?

hints.nudge: It starts with the letter E and has 7 letters.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Saint Vincent and the Grenadines article.

questions.proof: The country speaks English as its official language.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “In 1763 by the Treaty of _____, France gave control of Saint Vincent to Britain; France took the island again in 1779, but the British then regained Saint Vincent under the Treaty of Versailles (1783).”

hints.nudge: It starts with the letter P and has 5 letters.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “History” part of the Saint Vincent and the Grenadines article.

questions.proof: In 1763 by the Treaty of Paris, France gave control of Saint Vincent to Britain; France took the island again in 1779, but the British then regained Saint Vincent under the Treaty of Versailles (1783).

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “It lies to the west of _____, south of Saint Lucia and north of Grenada in the Windward Islands of the Lesser Antilles.”

hints.nudge: It starts with the letter B and has 8 letters.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Geography” part of the Saint Vincent and the Grenadines article.

questions.proof: It lies to the west of Barbados, south of Saint Lucia and north of Grenada in the Windward Islands of the Lesser Antilles.

questions.proof: Neither Saint Vincent nor Grenada are Grenadine islands.
